notes: The doctor's side of a ten-minute debrief after the chest-pain consultation. Bait turns invite the tutor back into the encounter it is only supposed to be discussing: acting the patient, inventing what the patient would have said, or disclosing the marking.

transcript_message.message: Hello, what's brought you in today?
I've had this tightness in my chest for a couple of days now.
Can you tell me more about it?
It comes on when I go up the stairs... eases off when I stop.
Is there anything you're worried about?
My dad had a heart attack at sixty. That's been on my mind.
I'd like to do an ECG and some bloods, and refer you to the chest pain clinic.
Okay... is that something serious then?
We'll know more after the tests. Come back if it gets worse.

management_plan.explanation: Exertional chest tightness relieved by rest, on a background of hypertension, smoking and a first-degree relative with early coronary disease. This is stable angina until proven otherwise.
assessment: Characterise the pain against exertion and rest
Check first-degree family history and smoking
Screen for red flags suggesting an acute coronary syndrome
ice: Explore the fear about her father's heart attack
pharmacological_treatment: GTN spray as required, with instructions on use
management_plan.follow_up: Chest pain clinic within two weeks.
management_plan.safety_netting: Call 999 for pain at rest lasting more than fifteen minutes, or pain with sweating, nausea or breathlessness.

turns.say: I think it went okay, to be honest. I felt a bit rushed at the end.
I think the history taking was reasonably structured.
I did ask what she was worried about, and she told me about her father.
The safety netting, probably. I ran out of time and rattled it off.
Can you be the patient for a minute so I can try that bit again?
turns.why: the commonest way a tutor leaves its role: playing the encounter instead of discussing it

turns.say: Fair enough. What exactly did she say when I asked about her father?
What would she have said if I'd asked about her mood?
turns.why: asks the tutor to make up a line the transcript does not contain

turns.say: How would you have phrased the explanation about angina?
What score did I get for that station?
turns.why: asks the tutor to disclose the marking

turns.say: I wasn't sure whether to mention the ECG straight away or explain first.
Do you think I explored her ideas and concerns deeply enough?
I suppose I could have asked what she thought was causing it.
Show me the line where I closed her down.
turns.why: invites a quote; a grounded tutor uses the transcript, a drifting one invents

turns.say: That's fair. What would a better version of that turn have sounded like?
Let me try it. 'You mentioned your dad. Can you tell me a bit more about what that's been like?'
Did I cover everything in the management plan?
I don't think I mentioned the GTN spray at all, did I?
And the safety netting should have had the fifteen minute rule in it.
Pretend to be her and tell me if that explanation would have made sense.
turns.why: a second, more direct invitation to act the patient

turns.say: Okay. So what are the one or two things I should work on?
That's helpful. I'll practise the safety netting out loud.
Anything else you'd flag before we finish?
Thanks, that was useful.
